searchText: The information cannot be derived without re-executing the transaction. Perhaps the real question is, "what is the point of including receipts at all" since technically they are derived information (re-execute the block). Why do you need to reexecute? You should be able to to lookup the tx by hash, get the feeCap and tip then lookup block base fee? There was some reason I thought... Maybe it was just because you needed the block, and I didn't want to assume that the user would have a block when they had a receipt, but maybe that isn't a reasonable assumption? Given that receipts don’t have the gas price in them at all, I don’t think requiring users to also fetch the block would be too burdensome Clients could also have a db table that indexes txs effective gas prices if users desire. I don’t see a reason to include it in a consensus structure honestly Prior to 1559, transaction + receipt was enough information to figure out gas cost. After 1559, transaction + block + receipt is necessary unless we add something to the receipt. I'm fairly ambivalent. I just worry about creating new dependencies when we could just add an RLP encoded number to receipts. Not a huge deal either way, so if people feel particularly strongly I'll probably back down. I don't think we should include the `effectiveGasPrice` in the tx receipt; it only makes the implementation somewhat more complex, and we can calculate these fields with some RPC calls. We also do not include whatever value is returned into the receipt for instance, it is a bit of a hassle but we can still re-calculate the return value if we want. In what way does it make the implementation more complex? Yeah, receipts definitely have less data in them than many would like! I was merely trying to not *remove* a capability that was previously present given a specific set of data. It requires a new receipt payload format (the first). In geth there are a few different versions of how receipts are stored on disk and those would be updated. So it isn’t exactly simple. Obviously I don’t want to current implementations to dictate protocol changes that *should* happen, it just doesn’t feel like we need this new field in the receipt Mechanisms for storing different receipts will be needed in London, so it seems like at best you are kicking the can down the road 4 months. I'm mostly convinced of removing it from receipts. I just think that particular argument is not a good one. Your phrasing of the situation in your PR description was good and convincing. "everything in receipt requires re-execution of the transaction/block". Sorry, if it wasn’t clear it’s much easier to support a new “type” (in geth at least) than actually changing the fields present But again, the main motivation is what I put in the PR This would be a new type. It makes it more complex in the sense that we have to add more logic when compared to the current version of the EIP It is logic you will need in London though. Yes but the actual field are the same, so all the structures and logic are reused With 2718, clients should be thinking of ways to make new transaction and receipt types easy or you'll suffer with each new transaction type. Agreed 🙂
